questions.stem: Which of the following structures is part of the portal triad found in the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explanation: The portal triad consists of the portal vein, hepatic artery proper, and common bile duct. The celiac trunk and SMA are separate arterial branches.

questions.stem: The phrenic nerve supplies which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve (C3‑C5) innervates the diaphragm. It does not supply the sternum, liver, or gallbladder.

questions.stem: Which artery gives rise to the right gastroepiploic artery?
questions.explanation: The right gastroepiploic artery is a branch of the gastroduodenal artery, not the right gastric or hepatic arteries.

questions.stem: The lesser sac is located posterior to which structure?
questions.explanation: The lesser sac lies posterior to the stomach and anterior to the pancreas; it is not posterior to the duodenum or spleen.

questions.stem: Which of the following veins drains the lower limb into the inferior vena cava?
questions.explanation: The femoral vein joins the external iliac to form the common iliac, which then joins the internal iliac to form the IVC. The other veins drain into the femoral.

questions.stem: The ligament of Treitz is a suspensory ligament of which part of the gastrointestinal tract?
questions.explanation: The ligament of Treitz suspends the duodenojejunal flexure, marking the transition from duodenum to jejunum.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the hepatoceliac trunk?
questions.explanation: The celiac trunk is the origin of the common hepatic, splenic, and left gastric arteries; the gastroduodenal is a branch of the common hepatic.

questions.stem: The left colic artery supplies which segment of the colon?
questions.explanation: The left colic artery supplies the descending colon; the ascending colon is supplied by the ileocolic artery.

questions.stem: Which of the following nerves innervates the external anal sphincter?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve provides somatic innervation to the external anal sphincter.

questions.stem: The suprapubic region is located over which bone?
questions.explanation: The suprapubic region lies over the pubic symphysis, part of the ilium.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the largest lymph node group in the axilla?
questions.explanation: Apical axillary nodes are the largest and drain the breast and upper limb.

questions.stem: The median arcuate ligament compresses which structure when it is abnormally tight?
questions.explanation: A tight median arcuate ligament can compress the celiac trunk, causing celiac artery compression syndrome.

questions.stem: Which of the following arteries supplies the pyloric antrum?
questions.explanation: The right gastric artery supplies the pyloric antrum; the left gastric supplies the lesser curvature.

questions.stem: The ligamentum teres hepatis is a remnant of which fetal structure?
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres is the fibrous remnant of the fetal umbilical vein.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explanation: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal triad: common bile duct, portal vein, and hepatic artery. The celiac trunk lies higher in the abdomen and is not within this ligament.

questions.stem: The left colic flexure is supplied by which artery?
questions.explanation: The left colic artery, a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery, supplies the splenic flexure. The other arteries supply different segments.

questions.stem: Which nerve innervates the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve (C3-C5) provides motor innervation to the diaphragm. Vagus supplies abdominal viscera, accessory supplies sternocleidomastoid, hypoglossal supplies tongue.

questions.stem: The round ligament of the uterus is a remnant of which embryonic structure?
questions.explanation: The round ligament derives from the gubernaculum, which is a remnant of the yolk sac. Allantois forms the urachus; urogenital sinus forms bladder; fallopian tube is separate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common site of splenic rupture after blunt abdominal trauma?
questions.explanation: The lower pole of the spleen is most frequently injured due to its mobility and lack of protective ribs. Upper and mid poles are less exposed.

questions.stem: The pharyngeal constrictor muscles are innervated by which cranial nerve?
questions.explanation: CN X (vagus) supplies all pharyngeal constrictors. CN V supplies muscles of mastication, VII facial, IX glossopharyngeal.

questions.stem: Which structure passes posterior to the pancreas?
questions.explanation: The portal vein runs posterior to the neck of the pancreas. Splenic vein is anterior; SMA is anterior; CBD is anterior.

questions.stem: The median arcuate ligament is a fibrous arch formed by the diaphragmatic crura over which artery does it pass?
questions.explanation: The median arcuate ligament arches over the celiac trunk. It does not cross the SMA, renal arteries, or aorta.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a component of the thoracic duct?
options: Lymph from the left upper limb
Lymph from the right lower limb
Lymph from the left lower limb
Lymph from the right upper limb
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct drains lymph from the left upper limb, left lower limb, and right lower limb. Lymph from the right upper limb drains via the right lymphatic duct.

questions.stem: The inferior vena cava is formed by the union of which two veins?
questions.explanation: The IVC is formed by the confluence of the common iliac veins. External and internal iliac veins join to form the common iliac.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct order of layers in the abdominal wall from superficial to deep?
options: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, transversalis fascia, peritoneum
Skin, subcutaneous tissue, transversalis fascia, muscle, peritoneum
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, transversalis fascia, peritoneum. The other options misplace fascia or muscle.

questions.stem: The ligament of Treitz is a tendinous band that attaches the duodenum to which structure?
questions.explanation: The ligament of Treitz attaches the duodenum to the mesentery, marking the duodenojejunal flexure. It does not attach to the intestines themselves.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the portal triad?
questions.explanation: The portal triad consists of the common hepatic duct, portal vein, and hepatic artery. The celiac trunk is a higher arterial source.

questions.stem: The right gastric artery typically arises from which vessel?
questions.explanation: The right gastric artery usually branches from the common hepatic artery. It does not arise from the gastroepiploic, left gastric, or splenic arteries.

questions.stem: Which of the following arteries supplies the majority of the blood to the spleen?
questions.explanation: The splenic artery, a branch of the celiac trunk, is the main arterial supply to the spleen. The other arteries supply different abdominal organs.

questions.stem: The left gastric vein drains into which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: The left gastric vein joins the portal vein, contributing to portal circulation. It does not drain into systemic veins.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explanation: The portal vein is within the hepatoduodenal ligament; the celiac trunk lies proximal to it and is not part of the ligament.

questions.stem: The phrenic nerve supplies motor innervation to which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve originates from C3-C5 and supplies the diaphragm. It does not innervate the other listed muscles.

questions.stem: Which of the following lymph nodes is the first station for lymphatic drainage of the lower limb?
questions.explanation: Inguinal lymph nodes are the primary drainage point for the lower limb. Popliteal nodes drain the knee region but are not the first station.

questions.stem: The median arcuate ligament is a fibrous arch that surrounds which artery?
questions.explanation: The median arcuate ligament encircles the celiac trunk. It does not involve the other arteries listed.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT a component of the hepatopancreatic ampulla?
questions.explanation: The hepatopancreatic ampulla (ampulla of Vater) consists of the common bile duct, pancreatic duct, and duodenum. The stomach is not involved.

questions.stem: The left renal vein receives a direct tributary from which of the following veins?
options: Renal vein of the right kidney
questions.explanation: The left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein. The right renal vein drains into the IVC, not the left renal vein.

questions.stem: The ligamentum teres hepatis is a remnant of which embryonic structure?
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres hepatis is the fibrous remnant of the fetal umbilical vein. It is not related to arteries or lymphatics.

questions.stem: Which of the following nerves provides sensory innervation to the skin over the anterior abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: The iliohypogastric nerve supplies the lower anterior abdominal wall. The other nerves supply different regions.

questions.stem: The right hepatic artery typically arises from which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: The right hepatic artery usually branches from the celiac trunk. It does not arise from the SMA or portal vein.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the posterior abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: The external oblique muscle is part of the anterior abdominal wall, not the posterior.
